title: The Second Letter of John
subtitle: Iōannou B, “Second of John”
description: A single page from “the elder” to “the chosen lady and her children”, one of the two shortest books in the Bible. In thirteen verses it gathers up the message of 1 John: walk in the truth, love one another as you were commanded from the beginning, and beware of deceivers who do not confess Jesus Christ as one who has come in the flesh. Do not give such teachers your home and your blessing; and the rest, the elder says, he would rather say face to face, so that your joy may be complete. In the Open Word Bible, a new translation from the Greek given freely to the public domain, with an introduction to the letter’s shape and meaning and a conclusion on where to read next.

qa.question: What is the Second Letter of John?
qa.answer: The twenty-fourth book of the New Testament and one of its two shortest, thirteen verses written by “the elder” to “the chosen lady and her children”. It urges its readers to keep living in the truth and loving one another, warns them against deceivers who deny that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and tells them not to welcome such teachers into their homes. It closes with the hope of a visit face to face.

qa.question: Who wrote 2 John, and who is “the chosen lady”?
qa.answer: The writer calls himself only “the elder”. The church has long linked him with John the apostle, author of the Gospel and of 1 John, whose language the letter shares; some ancient and modern readers think he was John the Elder, a disciple whom Papias distinguished from the apostle. “The chosen lady” may be a Christian woman in whose house a church met, but most readers take her to be a church, with its members as her children, since the letter ends with greetings from “your chosen sister’s children” (1:13).

qa.question: Why does 2 John say not to welcome false teachers into your home?
qa.answer: Early Christians met in homes, and travelling teachers relied on believers for lodging and a hearing. To receive a teacher into your house was to give him a platform in the church that met there, and to send him on with a greeting was to recommend him to the next. The elder tells the church not to do this for those who deny that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh (1:7–11). He is not forbidding ordinary kindness to people who disagree, and Christians weigh differently how the instruction applies today.

qa.question: Which translation of the Bible is this?
qa.answer: The Open Word Bible, a new translation made directly from the Greek and dedicated to the public domain, printed here at its Balanced level, which aims to be accurate and to read naturally aloud. The reasoning behind each of its sentences, with the Greek beside it, is published at openwordbible.org. The introduction and conclusion were written for this edition.
